method: Weekly PubMed search for recent peer-reviewed autism research aligned with JourHelp's support, accommodation, sensory, masking, burnout, communication, diagnosis, and quality-of-life goals.

studies.title: Parenting behaviours and autistic children's internalizing and externalizing symptoms: a protocol of a systematic review and meta-analysis.
studies.authors: Andrews K, Masood N, Mansoor A et al.
studies.preview: Autistic children can experience elevated levels of emotional and behavioural problems, which adversely impact their psychosocial functioning. Positive parenting behaviours can significantly shape children's emotional and behavioural developmental trajectories.

studies.title: Prospective memory and executive functions in adults across the wider autistic spectrum.
studies.preview: Prospective memory (PM) refers to the cognitive ability of remembering to execute an intended action in the future. Empirical evidence indicates reduced PM performance in autistic individuals.

studies.title: Advances in supporting development in autistic children and youth.
studies.authors: Penner M, Zwaigenbaum L, Piroddi N et al.
studies.preview: Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition with varied trajectories through the lifespan, leading to individualized patterns of strengths and challenges. Longitudinal autism cohort studies show the importance of developmental and adaptive skills starting in the early years, followed by emerging co-occurring conditions...

studies.title: Measuring quality of life in autistic children and young people: comparing the performance of common generic health related quality of life instruments.
studies.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
studies.authors: Constable L, O'Loughlin R, Jones R et al.
studies.preview: To assess the comparative measurement performance of commonly used paediatric health related quality of life (HRQoL) instruments in autistic children. The sample was 510 autistic children aged 5-18 years from the Australian Paediatric Multi-Instrument Comparison study.

studies.title: Untangling Sex and Gender Differences in Impression Management and Associated Autism Features in French Autistic Adults.
studies.journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
studies.authors: Ai W, Anchordoqui A, Bogdanova O et al.
studies.preview: Some autistic individuals camouflage their behavioral differences, a phenomenon that overlaps with general impression management (IM). Few studies have examined IM in autistic people, particularly outside English-speaking countries.
